column1: # mandatory-step-discovery.tsv — the DISPOSITION LEDGER that turns the
# mandatory-step birth rule from an opt-in registry into a CLASS
# (temperloop#1448, epic #1616).
# WHAT PROBLEM THIS FILE SOLVES. mandatory-step-registry.tsv is opt-in: a
# mandatory declaration nobody registered would not be failed, it would simply
# not be checked — the same "somebody has to remember" hole one level up from
# the defect the rule exists to close. So
# workflows/scripts/validate-mandatory-step-signal.sh ENUMERATES every
# mandatory-marker line in claude/commands/*.md mechanically and fails any that
# has no disposition anywhere. This file is where a discovered line that is
# deliberately NOT registered records WHY. Silence stopped being a legal
# answer.
# Format: four TAB-separated columns; #-comments and blank lines ignored.
#   SPEC         repo-relative path of the claude/commands/*.md spec.
#   ANCHOR       a LITERAL substring of the discovered line. A row whose anchor
#                no longer appears in SPEC is LEDGER-STALE and fails — prune it
#                in the same change that reworded the prose.
#   DISPOSITION  `excluded` — the line is NOT a step-execution declaration (see
#                the gate's § THE SCOPE DECISION (a)): a constraint on how a
#                step behaves once running, a required argument or artifact
#                field, or prose that merely REFERENCES a mandatory rule
#                declared elsewhere. These fail loudly when violated; only a
#                step that never runs is silent, and that silence is all this
#                gate exists to break.
#                `pending` — it IS a step-execution declaration and has no
#                execution signal yet. SHRINK-ONLY RATCHET (see below).
#   REASON       required, non-empty, human-readable.
# THE `pending` RATCHET IS THE BIRTH RULE'S TEETH. A `pending` row present now
# but absent at the ratchet base ref is PENDING-GREW and fails. So the rows
# below are the pre-existing debt the rule was born owing, and the set can only
# shrink: a BRAND-NEW mandatory declaration cannot be parked here. It ships its
# signal in the same change, or it is `excluded` — a reviewable claim, visible
# in the diff, that it was never a step-execution declaration at all.
# SPEC
column2: ANCHOR
column4: REASON

column1: # ── pending: real step-execution declarations, no signal yet ────────────────
claude/commands/tidy.md
column2: ## Step 2 — Sensitivity scan (mandatory)
column4: A whole mandatory step of an UNATTENDED command with no per-run evidence that it ran: /tidy's own summary carries no scan tally, and a run that skipped it is indistinguishable from a run that scanned and found nothing. Needs a per-run tally (stubs scanned / flags parked) in the Step 6 summary before it can be registered.

column1: claude/commands/triage.md
column2: Step-1 intake-deferred line is the mandatory one every run
column4: A mandatory per-run EMISSION ("Intake deferral is always reported, never silent") that is itself the mitigation for an earlier silent-skip defect (foundation#164/#208) — and it has no signal of its own: emit-command-run.sh carries no deferred-count field, so an omitted line leaves no trace. Needs a `deferred` counter on the telemetry record.

column1: claude/commands/workshop.md
column2: first-run/uninstall persona run is **mandatory**
column4: The install-surface first-run/uninstall persona run is mandated as EXECUTED (explicitly outranking inspection), but /workshop emits nothing distinguishing an executed run from an inspected one. Needs an executed-vs-inspected field on the design brief before it can be registered.

column1: # ── excluded: not step-execution declarations ──────────────────────────────
# (a) Constraints on how a step BEHAVES once it is running. Violating one is
#     loud by construction — the step ran and its own output is wrong — which
#     is precisely what a step that never runs does not give you.
claude/commands/build.md
column2: **Selection rule (load-bearing, non-negotiable):**
column4: A ROUTING rule (operator-absent + ask-now → async backend), not a declaration that a step executes. It constrains which backend a question takes when the step runs; it cannot be silently skipped, only taken wrongly, and a wrong route shows up in the question that gets asked.

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: exit capture is mandatory whenever the gate is piped
column4: A HOW-TO-INVOKE constraint on §3e.5's gate call (pipefail + a dialect-safe exit read), not a declaration that §3e.5 runs. The step's own Pass/Fail verdict is the observable; this rule only governs how that verdict is read.

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: push-before-watch stays mandatory post-#605
column4: An ORDERING constraint between two steps that both already run (push, then watch CI). Violating it produces a 404-to-ERROR poll against an unpushed SHA, which is loud; it is not a step that can silently not happen.

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: The pin is **required, not optional** (#254)
column4: An ARGUMENT-SHAPE constraint (`ci-poll.sh --sha <pushed SHA>`), not a step execution. The re-poll step runs either way; the pin governs which SHA it watches.

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: never skips or rewrites a PR
column4: Not a mandatory declaration at all — the marker vocabulary's `never skip` matching "never skips or rewrites a PR", a sentence describing the conservative DEFAULT of the 4c conflict disposition. Flagging it would be the temperloop#1152 class (a guard firing on prose that merely contains its trigger word).

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: validate-mandatory-step-signal.sh`) never false-fails this gate
column4: Not a mandatory declaration at all — the marker vocabulary's `mandatory` matching inside the literal filename `validate-mandatory-step-signal.sh`, named (alongside two sibling validators) as an example of an origin/main-ratcheted gate the temperloop#1937 freshness rebase protects. The temperloop#1152 class again: a guard firing on prose that merely contains its trigger word, this time as a substring of a script's own name.

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: the pass is **recorded, not merely logged** (temperloop#1431)
column4: An ARTIFACT-FIELD constraint on §3e.6's own OUTPUT — the class-A PASS record (`park()`'s `activation: {…}` on the Workflow path, the hand-stamped `[m]` sentinel sub-line on the conversational one) — not a declaration that §3e.6 runs. Same shape as the assess.md `epic: <N>` row below: the thing that could go missing is a FIELD, and an unwritten field is visible in the record's own output, not silent. The marker also only trips here as an incidental CITATION to the kernel's § Mandatory-step birth rule (the sentence explains WHY the pass is recorded), never as an execution obligation stated in this gate's vocabulary — the temperloop#1152 class. §3e.6's class-A `proof:` declaration is a DIFFERENT line, registered on its own in mandatory-step-registry.tsv (plan-schema rule 13, guarded by test_plan.sh).

column1: claude/commands/assess.md
column2: **This is load-bearing, not optional, in epic-decomposition mode:**
column4: An ARTIFACT-FIELD constraint (`epic: <N>` must be in the plan frontmatter), not a step execution. Its absence is already caught downstream — build.md Step 2.6's backstop arm fires and mints a duplicate epic, which is visible on the board.

column1: # (b) Prose that merely REFERENCES a mandatory rule declared elsewhere. The
#     declaration these point at is dispositioned at its own site; flagging the
#     reference too would demand a second signal for one rule and make every

claude/commands/check-in.md

column4: A back-reference to tidy.md's own Step 2 declaration, which is dispositioned `pending` above. /check-in's step here is READING the surface that scan parks to, not running the scan.

column1: claude/commands/triage.md
column2: the same reasoning as the mandatory Step-1 intake-deferred line
column4: A back-reference to triage.md's own Step-1 declaration, dispositioned `pending` above; this sentence is about the pending-feedback tail note, which is explicitly optional ("print nothing when it is empty").

column1: claude/commands/workshop.md
column2: the mandatory rule that every finding cites a named principle
column4: A back-reference to a rule declared in an AGENT CHARTER (the reviewer's own output contract), which is outside this gate's scope — a pipeline STEP is a step of a workflow spec, not a reviewer's internal formatting rule.

column1: claude/commands/tidy.md
column2: the superseded "registry row mandatory" cost line
column4: Prose ABOUT the capture/backstop registry, quoting a superseded claim in order to record that it was superseded. Failing a doc for documenting its own subject is the temperloop#1152 defect class.

column1: claude/commands/assess.md
column2: review-agent availability is a MECHANICAL PROBE
column4: A HOW-TO-RESOLVE constraint on an existing step, not a declaration that a step executes. /assess Step 3 already declares its own review pass and carries its own signal (the Step 5 summary line, plus the cross-PR rollup workflows/scripts/workflow-reviewer-coverage.sh). This line only says that the AVAILABILITY question inside that pass is answered by agent_declared_state rather than by eye (temperloop#1462) — it cannot be silently skipped, only answered wrongly, and a wrong answer surfaces as a skip notice for an agent that would have spawned. Same shape as the two build.md exclusions above.

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: stalls the mandatory §3e reviewer pass with no operator watching
column4: A back-reference to §3e's own foundation#1007 declaration, which is registered with the `review: { mandatory_ok }` per-run tally as its signal. This clause is about which CALLERS supply reviewerRoutingTsv (temperloop#1992), not a second declaration that §3e runs.

column1: claude/commands/sweep.md
column2: stalls the mandatory §3e reviewer pass with no operator watching
column4: The same back-reference to build.md §3e's foundation#1007 declaration, made at the /sweep caller site to say why the reviewerRoutingTsv hand-off matters most on an unattended run. /sweep declares no reviewer step of its own.

column1: claude/commands/sweep.md
column2: **Degraded-routing rows (temperloop#2020).**
column4: A REPORT-RENDERING rule for /sweep's Step 4 block, not a declaration that a step executes. Its one marker word is a back-reference to build.md §3e's foundation#1007 command-doc rule, named only to say which routes SURVIVE a degraded reviewer-routing relay; the rule itself is declared and signalled at its own site (the review: { mandatory_ok } per-run tally). A missing row here is loud by construction — workflows/scripts/build/tests/test_workflow.sh's #2020 report-surface guard greps this section for routing_degraded and fails when it is absent.

column2: **Degraded-routing line (temperloop#2020).**
column4: The /fix half of the sweep.md row above, same shape and same reason: a REPORT-RENDERING rule for Step 7 whose only marker word back-references build.md §3e's foundation#1007 declaration (signalled at its own site), and which is itself guarded by the #2020 report-surface grep in workflows/scripts/build/tests/test_workflow.sh.

column1: claude/commands/build.md
column2: a **mandatory** one escalates `review-agent-timeout` carrying the computed tally

This clause documents the reviewAgentCeilingSecs hand-off's TIMEOUT DISPOSITION for that already-declared step (temperloop#2003) — advisory degrades, mandatory escalates — not a second declaration that a step executes. Same shape as the two §3e back-reference exclusions below.
